correctness.rationale: PASS: In A=D⊕J with J²=0, the r-th power of λ+a has arrow coefficient a_e sum_k λ_i^(r−1−k)λ_j^k. For d|q−1, a coefficient is free iff its endpoints receive distinct d-th roots; loops and equal endpoints force zero. Conjugation by 1+x acts independently on exactly those free arrows, proving single-class fibers. For pd, every radical coordinate is free because (1+J)^p=1. Möbius inversion gives exact orders and all possible orders divide p(q−1). Fortuin–Kasteleyn expansion is an exact finite identity; infinitely many prime powers congruent to 1 mod d yield polynomial interpolation and recover the Tutte polynomial, while the p-fiber determines total loops. An independent arithmetic checker exhaustively enumerated unit orders in 49 configurations, including F4, loops, multiple and opposite arrows, and the five-cycle. Finite checks do not establish the general theorem; the written proof does.

originality.rationale: PASS within investigated evidence: Sokal establishes only the classical Fortuin–Kasteleyn identity; Iovanov–Sistko classify maximal subalgebras; Qureshi–Reis treats power maps on abelian and flower groups. Accessible prior quiver-unit work determines a different Tutte specialization for commuting statistics, and incidence-algebra work addresses comparability graphs/idempotent tuples rather than exact unit orders for arbitrary quivers. Here the p-divisible and p-prime order strata, their conjugacy class sizes, and all-field recovery of the undirected Tutte polynomial are asserted together. Equivalence in older semidirect-product or ring-unit literature remains a recorded risk.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent torsion enumeration could be implicit in older semidirect-product/finite-algebra literature not retrieved by text searches.
Some small unit groups may belong to previously studied flower-group or affine-group classes; no novelty is claimed for their general power-map theory.
The Tutte recovery uses an established graph-polynomial transform. Its novelty claim is the identification and exact torsion-statistics bridge, not the transform.

value.rationale: PASS: The complete multiplicative order census and prime-to-characteristic conjugacy-class sizes are natural invariants of the unit groups of finite basic algebras. The all-field spectra recover the Tutte polynomial of the underlying nonloop multigraph and total loop multiplicity while rigorously exposing the orientation information they cannot retain. This quantitative reconstruction across arbitrary quivers goes beyond isolated numerical counts or a relabeling of the known Potts identity; its p-primary split supplies information unavailable from a prime-to-p color count alone.
